spec.section:
# WF-08/WF-07 isolated controller-loss restore drill
This fixture is the required R32-017 scenario, not a session-export-only example. The verified controller backup is `backup-manifest.json`; the old controller `ctrl-old` is absent/fenced and cannot be read during the drill. The backup includes coordination, ticket/workflow, dispatch/attempt, grants/policy, configuration, asset metadata, archive indexes, retention and credential references. It contains no secret material.
The fixture has two relevant sends: `send-complete-1` has a durable terminal report and must not be replayed; `att-uncertain-1` was admitted/dispatched with a lost response and cannot be classified during the drill. The replacement preserves its original identity, marks it `paused:uncertain`, holds capacity, records an escalation, and makes no replacement POST. It must return `503 controller_recovery_incomplete` before readiness and while the uncertain run remains unresolved.
`restore-report.json` is the expected evidence shape: new writer identity and fence, pre-readiness refusal, exactly one completed effect with no replay, held uncertain capacity, readable control/archive evidence, credential reattachment by reference only, and readiness still refused. After an authorized positive-stop decision or later proof of stop, the controller writes the durable reconciliation/release record, runs every readiness gate, and only then enables dispatch.
The archive/session-export distinction remains explicit: `chd-archive` payloads are opaque native session exports with checkpoint/gap manifests. They do not restore controller rooms, tickets, manifests, grants, reservations or configuration.
